subject: Re: Holdback policy and soft-rollback plan for Zipline packaging
messages:
From: Alyssa Moore <alyssa.moore@ziplinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging holdback & seat reshuffle options for pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood for inference. Procurement asked me to get clarity on two packaging points before we finish the pilot SOW:

1) Holdback policy: we want a clear definition for which features can be held back during pilot->GA and what the rollback / re-enable process looks like if a feature causes regressions.
2) Seat reshuffle: during the pilot we may need to move seats between teams (e.g., 10 seats from triage -> analytics) and want to understand prorate/credit mechanics and if you support seat pools.

Can you send options your team typically proposes (safety-net language, timing windows, credit math)? We also need a one-page summary for procurement that they can use for internal approvals.

Cheers,
Alyssa
Alyssa Moore
Head of Product, Zipline Health
(p) 415-555-0123

attachment: pilot_scope.pdf (pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa.moore@ziplinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging holdback & seat reshuffle options for pilot

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear ask. I'll paste a short options overview below and Ben/Karthik will attach the detailed worksheet. We can turn this into a one-page procurement summary as requested.

Quick options overview (high level):
- Soft holdback (recommended for pilots): allow 1-2 non-critical features gated behind a flag; automatic rollback window of 24 hours to previous configuration; 30-day monitoring SLA before GA.
- Hard feature exclusion: exclude high-risk features from the pilot build; requires config change and 5 business day rollback window.
- Seat pool approach: create a 20% buffer pool for pilot seats; seats moved into pool are credited at a sliding prorate (monthly basis).

Ben will share numbers and the spreadsheet with prorate math + suggested safety-net wording. Karthik, can you include the routing & SLA carveouts (e.g., what we do if model quantization reduces latency but impacts accuracy)?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call Monday to finalize language for procurement.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging holdback & seat reshuffle options for pilot — options + numbers attached

Hi Alyssa —

Attached are two artifacts: (1) zipline_pack_options_v3.xlsx — the prorate math, holdback tiers, and an example rollback SLA; (2) zipline_mutual_action_plan.docx — a suggested one-page procurement summary / MAP. Key points called out here:

1) Holdback tiers (pilot):
  - Tier A (soft): 1 feature gated, immediate rollback via remote flag, rollback testing window 24 hours, no credit.
  - Tier B (hard): features excluded from pilot, re-enable requires config deploy and 5 business-day rollback test window, 5% credit applied to first invoice if rework required.

2) Rollback triggers & QA: automatic rollback triggered by either accuracy degradation > 3% on agreed evals or latency spike beyond 2x baseline for 1 hour. We propose a 48-hour incident review window before credits apply.

3) Seat reshuffle mechanics:
  - Seat pool: create a pilot pool equal to 15% of committed seats. Seats moved into pool return credits prorated daily (credit = monthly seat price * remaining days / 30).
  - One-off reshuffles: allow up to 25% of seats to move between teams once per 30-day period without penalty; beyond that, standard prorate applies.

4) Pricing impact & pilot discount: the safety-net adds operational overhead; for Tier A we don't change list price but we can offer a 5% pilot discount on committed tokens for a 60-day pilot. For Tier B (hard exclusion) we can offer a 10% concession if Zipline signs a 12-month committed plan at pilot close.

Please review the sheet — the cover tab includes sample numbers for a 200-seat/6M token pilot. Happy to walk through.

Attachments: zipline_pack_options_v3.xlsx (xlsx), zipline_mutual_action_plan.docx (docx)

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging holdback & seat reshuffle options for pilot — quick Qs

Thanks Ben — this looks good and the spreadsheet is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before procurement: 

- If we choose Tier A soft holdback, can you confirm the exact SLAs around rollback time (we need to guarantee re-enable in < 24 hours for our clinical flows)?
- For the 5% credit in Tier B, is that applied as an invoice credit or as an up-front discount? Procurement prefers invoice credits.
- On seats: our security team requires seat movement logs and audit trails for compliance — can Redwood provide an audit export for seat reassignment events?

Also — procurement is pushing for a 10% pilot discount off the committed token rate for the 60-day pilot. Is that something we can consider if we sign a brief MSA with the Tier B exclusion?

Would like to finalize language by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Alyssa

Alyssa / Mike —

Thanks for the quick review and helpful procurement points. Answers inline below and next steps: 

- Rollback SLA (Tier A): we confirm re-enable via flag within 8 hours for high-priority clinical flows; 24 hours for non-critical. We'll include an escalation path (pager + 2-hr on-call response) for clinical incidents in the SOW.
- 5% credit: invoice credit applied to the first post-pilot invoice (explicit in MAP).
- Seat audit logs: yes — Redwood will provide a CSV audit export for any seat reassignment event with timestamp, actor, and source IP. We will add that to the MAP appendix.
- Pilot discount ask (10%): we can offer 8% off committed token rate for a 60-day pilot when signing a 12-month MSA that includes Tier B exclusion. If Zipline signs only a pilot MSA we can do 5% + the Tier A soft holdback.

Next steps: Ben / Karthik / Lauren will update the MAP and the spreadsheet to reflect invoice-credit language and the 8% vs 5% options. Can we set a 30-min call tomorrow at 11am PT to finalize? If that works I'll share a short procurement one-pager and a DocuSign MSA preview.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
